shower.thought: The person you were ten years ago would be shocked by what you've accepted as normal.
You spend your whole life learning how to be human, and then you die.
Confidence is just fear that decided to stop announcing itself.
We call it "sleeping in" but really we're just admitting we were tired from being awake.
The things that scare you most are usually the things that matter most.
You can't remember most of your life, which means you've already forgotten who you were.
Boredom might just be your brain telling you that you've outgrown something.
We judge people by their worst moment and ourselves by our intentions.
The people who say "I don't care what people think" usually care the most—they're just tired.
Money is just a really popular form of agreement.
Your laugh is the only sound your body makes that you can't hear the way others hear it.
We fear being alone less than we fear being lonely with someone.
Every time you learn something new, you have to unlearn something you were confident about.
The saddest part of growing up isn't that life gets harder—it's that you stop expecting it to.
You've never actually touched anything; you're just experiencing forces pushing against each other.
People don't leave relationships because of one thing—they leave because they stopped being willing to stay.
Wanting to be better is the only evidence you're not as bad as you think.
The gap between who you want to be and who you are is called your life.
Your body is the only home you can never leave, which is either comforting or terrifying.
We spend so much energy on what people think of us that we forget to think about what we think of them.

motivational.thought: The best time to plant a tree was 20 years ago. The second best time is now. — Chinese Proverb
Your life is not waiting for you to figure it out. It's waiting for you to live it. — Unknown
Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most. — Unknown
The man who moves a mountain begins by carrying away small stones. — Confucius
You can't think your way into a new way of living. You have to live your way into a new way of thinking. — Unknown
Everything you want is on the other side of fear. — Jack Canfield
The obstacle is the way. — Marcus Aurelius
Most people overestimate what they can do in a year and underestimate what they can do in five. — Unknown
You are not behind. You are not lost. You are exactly where you need to be, learning what you need to learn. — Unknown
Done is better than perfect. — Voltaire
The only person you should try to be better than is the person you were yesterday. — Unknown
Your circumstances don't define you. Your response to them does. — Unknown
The gap between who you are and who you want to be is closed by what you do. — Bill Phillips
Regret is the price of inaction. — Unknown
To be unstoppable, you have to be willing to be uncomfortable. — Unknown
Progress is not about becoming someone else. It's about becoming more of who you already are. — Unknown
What lies behind us and what lies before us are tiny matters compared to what lies within us. — Ralph Waldo Emerson
The person who says it cannot be done should not interrupt the person doing it. — Chinese Proverb
Mistakes are proof that you're trying. — Unknown
Your past does not determine your future unless you live in it. — Unknown

darkjoke.thought:
I told my wife she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My grandfather said, "Your generation is too reliant on technology."
I unplugged his life support to prove him wrong.
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.
The worst time to have a heart attack is during a game of charades.

I said to my friend, "I think you're a pessimist."
He said, "No, I'm a realist."
We both were right—he jumped anyway.

My wife accused me of being too materialistic.
I said that's ridiculous and told her to stop interfering with my inheritance planning.

I tried to make a belt out of herbs once.
It was a waist of thyme, but at least I didn't commit suicide about it.

My therapist asked me to talk about my childhood.
Turns out that's billable, so I've got a lot to say.

I'm reading a book on anti-gravity.
It's impossible to put down, which is why I'm using it as a suicide note.

People keep asking me if I believe in life after death.
I told them, "I don't know, but based on my dating history, I believe in life after love."

I used to be addicted to soap, but I'm clean now.
The withdrawal wasn't pretty though—I was foaming at the mouth and everything.

My wife left me because I'm obsessed with astronomy.
She said I needed to focus on what's in front of me, not what's light-years away.
Fair point, but Jupiter's really hard to ignore.

I asked the funeral director why he seemed so sad all the time.
He said, "Job security."

My doctor told me I need to watch my drinking.
So now I drink in front of a mirror.

I told my boss I was feeling suicidal at work.
He said, "That's the spirit!"
I think we have different definitions.

The problem with time travel is that you can never change the past.
Though watching my parents meet and considering the alternatives does make me wonder.

I have a tattoo that says "No Ragrets."
Ironically, it's my biggest one.

They say money can't buy happiness.
But it can buy a jet ski—have you ever seen someone frown on a jet ski?
My neighbor did, right before he hit a rock.

My wife said I was being insensitive about her miscarriage.
I said, "At least we know the equipment works."

I joined a support group for people with short-term memory loss.
I love it there—I get to make new friends every single meeting.
